subject.title: feat: add Podman agent sandbox backend

question: Should `sandbox.allowBackends: ["docker"]` authorize execution through Podman when the Docker CLI is absent, or must the effective Podman engine be explicitly authorized?
rationale: Docker and Podman have different runtime, isolation, connection, user-mapping, and operational semantics; automation cannot decide whether the backend allowlist represents configured product identity or the engine that actually enforces the sandbox.

options.title: Require effective-engine authorization
options.body: Allow Docker-to-Podman fallback only when policy also authorizes `podman`, otherwise fail with an actionable configuration message.

options.title: Authorize the container family
options.body: Keep `allowBackends: ["docker"]` sufficient for fallback, but explicitly document and test that Docker authorization includes the supported Podman implementation.

options.title: Remove implicit fallback
options.body: Keep Docker behavior unchanged and require users to configure `backend: "podman"` whenever they want Podman.

recommendation.title: Require effective-engine authorization
recommendation.body: Allow Docker-to-Podman fallback only when policy also authorizes `podman`, otherwise fail with an actionable configuration message.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes the semantics of the pluggable sandbox architecture and policy boundary introduced in this area.
